reason: Passes the feasibility and schedule lens because it is not a pipeline mechanism. Nothing enters any submission notebook, so the byte-identical-when-off, fail-soft and hidden-runtime checks do not apply (0 s of the ~4 h headroom). It uses no LB slot, no GPU quota and no dummy or exp60 gate. The inputs already exist and check out: the CLI download works (scratchpad lb/...2026-09-25T16_52_13.csv, 3,904 teams), and the idea's numbers reproduce exactly. Blocks: 0.956 = ranks 77-96, 0.955 = 97-129, 0.954 = 130-192 (63 teams), 0.953 = 193-448 (256 teams). We are rank 149 at 0.954 with 37 submissions. Medal cutoffs: gold ~17, silver ~195, bronze ~390. Within each score block the order does not follow LastSubmissionDate: 28 of 62 adjacent pairs in the 0.954 block are out of time order, and 84 of 255 in the 0.953 block. That fits ordering by the unrounded score. It is only suggestive, because LastSubmissionDate is the team's latest submission, not the one that scored. The 27 Sep ~09:00 UTC diff falls before R8 (12:00). It costs ~0.3 agent-hours and needs no slot. Three conditions keep it inside the rules. (1) The pre-registration says §e/§f are applied, not rewritten, after scores are known, so this may only annotate status and finals reasoning; it must not change the F1/F2 selection rule. (2) Seeing sub-0.001 gaps must not start knob ladders or near-copy picks at 0.001 (R7, R9); R3/R4 stay as registered, and the idea says so itself. (3) Public ranks come from one public embryo and are a weak proxy for private ranks, so the rank line is information only.
fix: Keep it as information only. (a) Add one line to the daily status table and to CONTEXT.md: our rank, the edges of the 0.953 and 0.954 blocks, the score at rank ~195 (silver) and ~390 (bronze), and the team count. Recompute the 5%/10%/10+0.2% cutoffs from the team count on the day finals are ticked, not from today's 3,904. (b) Save a dated `kaggle competitions leaderboard --download` CSV next to experiments/lb_poll/ on 26 Sep and at 27 Sep ~09:00 UTC (before R8), and diff it against the 16:52 file to find new 0.955+ entries and public x138 descendants. Ranking CSV rows by score does not reveal unrounded values. (c) Write down that this changes no R1-R10 or §f decision and that it adds no ladders.
realistic_gain: 0 on the score. The value is decision hygiene: it confirms that the silver cutoff (~195) sits on the top edge of the 0.953 block and the bronze cutoff (~390) inside it. That supports the existing §f(iv) reason why F1 must not be a byte copy of x138, and flags a new public successor in time to react before R8. Cost ~0.3 h, no slots, no GPU, no hidden runtime.
